suggestions.title: Hip thrust debuts today — pick its opening load before you leave the house

rationale.science: A new lift's first day is for setting a starting number, not testing a limit: open about two reps shy of failure and the weight you write down is one you can build on next week (RIR-based load selection; Schoenfeld 2017 on what makes a hard set count).
rationale.data: The app still has no opening load for the hip thrust this morning — fifth day this card has been up, and today is the lower day it debuts. Last lower day, 8/14, it was skipped.
rationale.relationship: In your file, debuts without a chosen number end as a skip (hip thrust, 8/14) or as a number that later had to be taken back (hack squat's 170). A weight picked at the kitchen table costs nothing and turns today's first sets into a starting point that holds.

suggestions.predict: Pick it before the session and the debut opens at 1–2 reps in reserve and stands as a clean baseline. Walk in blank and I expect another skip, or a number we end up correcting.

suggestions.title: Fill in Thursday — rough numbers, five minutes. It is the one blank day under this morning's verdict.

rationale.science: Keeping the log itself is the strongest single predictor of losing on plan — gaps get filled by guesswork, and guesswork flatters (Alhassan 2008 on adherence as the meta-lever).
rationale.data: Thursday 8/20 has no food, steps or sleep behind it. Wednesday's blank was filled within a day of being asked — the sixth fill-in in a row that converted inside 24 hours.
rationale.relationship: The scale moved two pounds in two days while you were sick; how much of that was fat is decided by the intake record around it. Thursday is that record — and it closes the 'weekdays logged clean' condition the Friday call was graded under.

suggestions.predict: Filled tonight — the streak says inside a day — and the Friday call's asterisk clears; the weekend read stands on whole data.

suggestions.title: Three machines might be training the short half of the muscle — answer three questions in SETUP

rationale.science: Training a muscle at long lengths grows it measurably faster per set than at short lengths — the strongest machine-selection finding in the current literature, though the trained-lifter cohorts are small.
rationale.data: Your calf raise, triceps machine and ham curl are the three lifts where the answer is unknown; the check is three questions in SETUP and changes nothing until you say so. Still unanswered since yesterday.
rationale.relationship: If any of the three is the short-length version, every set on it has been buying less than it should — on a cut, where sets are expensive, knowing is free and switching is where the same effort pays more.

suggestions.predict: Three answers in SETUP inside a couple of days; if any machine turns out short-length, a switch proposal follows with the science attached.
